newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta Fed's Guynn sees US economy slowing by '98.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta Fed's Guynn sees US economy slowing by '98.

text.p: The U.S. economy will slow toward the end of this year and into 1998, but gross domestic product in 1997 might still grow faster than in 1996, according to Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank President Jack Guynn.

GDP growth "in 1997 could well exceed the 2.5-percent growth of last year," said Guynn in a speech to the New Orleans Rotary Club. Guynn added he sees "continued good growth with low inflation and low unemployment" and "a slowing in the pace of the national economy going into late 1997 and early 1998."
Calling the economy's performance since 1991 "extraordinary," Guynn said strong consumer spending underpins the current expansion.
"Consumer spending is leading the way," he said.

Responding to criticism of the Fed's hike in the federal funds rate on March 25 despite little or no sign of increase in most inflation measures, Guynn restated the Fed's forward looking view on inflation.
The central bank "must take preemptive action against inflation acceleration," because "waiting for evidence of inflation...virtually guarantees we will always be behind the curve."

Guynn acknowledged that Fed officials are currently debating whether "wage increases are justified by increases in labor productivity or coming from robust demand and indicate monetary policy is too loose."
